# Okkanta Saṁyutta (SN 25)

**ID:** SN 25  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Okkanta Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0303m.mul3.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0303m.mul3.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In Abhidharma studies, scholars such as Ryūjō Yamada have cited the tenfold groupings found in the *Okkanta Saṁyutta* as potential early scriptural precursors to systematic Abhidharma classifications of mental factors (*mahābhūmika*) [Gyatso 1992; Willemen et al. 1998].

**Sources**

- [Flores 2008] Ralph Flores, Buddhist Scriptures as Literature: Sacred Rhetoric and the Uses of Theory (2008) — Noted the distinction between faith-followers and dhamma-followers in SN 25.1.
- [Giustarini] Giustarini, Faith and Renunciation in Early Buddhism: Saddhā and Nekkhamma — Discussed the role of faith and renunciation across suttas of the Okkantasamyutta.
- [Gyatso 1992] Janet Gyatso (ed.), In the Mirror of Memory (1992), contribution by Collett Cox — Reported Yamada's analysis of SN 25 as a scriptural precedent for tenfold Abhidharma classifications of mental factors.
- [Willemen et al. 1998] Charles Willemen, Bart Dessein, and Collett Cox, Sarvāstivāda Buddhist Scholasticism (1998) — Cited Yamada's identification of SN 25's tenfold categories as precedents for Abhidharma classifications.
